description: ADsD identifier of the record, such as X301492. The digit after X is the ADART volume, and the rest encodes the ADART number.
ADsD project that holds the record. Values are adsd/adart1, adsd/adart2 and adsd/adart3, for ADART I, II and III.
ADART number of the record as the catalogue gives it, such as AD -261A.

First year of the published date. The catalogue writes a Babylonian year over two Julian years, such as 262/1, and this column holds 262. The published year in astronomical numbering is 1 minus this value. The file stores it as a float.

Second year of the published date, such as 261 for 262/1. It is the Julian year in which the Babylonian year ends. For the range 303 to 301 BCE of X103021, it holds 301. The file stores it as a float.
Year of the published date in the ancient count, as the catalogue gives it. Examples are SE 50 for year 50 of the Seleucid Era and ArtII 42 for a regnal year of Artaxerxes II.
Museum number of the tablet, such as BM 41690. A plus sign joins the numbers of the fragments that form one tablet.
Babylonian months that the tablet records, as the catalogue lists them. Brackets mark a break in the tablet.
Comments of the editors, from the catalogue. Some identify an eclipse with a date or note an error in the tablet. Empty when the catalogue has none.
Publication of a hand copy of the tablet, such as LBAT 249. Empty when the catalogue gives none.
Publication of a photograph of the tablet, such as ADART I plate 66. Empty when the catalogue gives none.
Accession number of the tablet in the museum, as the catalogue gives it.
Historical period, from the catalogue. Values are Neo-Assyrian, Neo-Babylonian, Achaemenid, Hellenistic and Parthian.
Place where the tablet was found, from the catalogue. Values are Babylon and Uruk.
East longitude of the provenience, from its Pleiades coordinate in the catalogue.
North latitude of the provenience, from its Pleiades coordinate in the catalogue.
Number of text lines that ADsD gives for the record. It is 0 when ADsD has no text.
English translation of the record, with one tablet line on each text line. Empty when ADsD has no translation. Dating reads only this column of the corpus.
ADsD identifier of the record that the line belongs to.
ADsD project of the record, adsd/adart1, adsd/adart2 or adsd/adart3.
Line label of the edition. o 5' is line 5' of the obverse, and r 4 is line 4 of the reverse. Other prefixes, such as b.e., name an edge.
Transliteration of the line, as ADsD gives it.
English translation of the line. Empty when the record has no translation.
Lemmatization of the line, which glosses each word. Only records that ADsD gives as transliteration without a translation have it. Empty for all other records.

Babylonian year, labeled by the Julian year in which it begins. It runs from -625, or 626 BCE, to 75, or AD 75. Each row is one month of this year.
Year label that Parker and Dubberstein print. Ac is the accession year and a number is a regnal year. Under the Seleucid Era heading, the number is the Seleucid Era year.

Position of the month in its year, from 1 to 12, or to 13 in a year with an extra month. In a year with VI2, position 7 is VI2.

Day of the Julian month, from 1 to 31, of the first day of the Babylonian month. It is not a Julian Day Number. The Babylonian day began at sunset, and the date is that of its daylight part.

Number of the eclipse in the NASA Five Millennium Catalog of its kind.
Canon plate number from the NASA solar catalogue. Empty for lunar eclipses. The file stores it as a float.
Kind of eclipse, lunar or solar.
Year of greatest eclipse, from the catalogue.
astro_year as a label, such as 700 BCE or AD 5.
Month of greatest eclipse, from 1 to 12, in the Julian calendar, as the catalogue gives it.
Day of the month of greatest eclipse, from the catalogue.
Hour of greatest eclipse in dynamical time, from the catalogue.
Minute of greatest eclipse in dynamical time.
Second of greatest eclipse in dynamical time.
Julian Date of greatest eclipse in dynamical time, from the catalogue date and time.
Julian Date of greatest eclipse in Universal Time. It is jd minus the catalogue Delta T.
Delta T that the catalogue gives, the difference between dynamical time and Universal Time.
One standard error of Delta T, 0.8 u squared seconds with u in centuries from AD 1820. The local trials use Delta T minus and plus this value.
Lunation number from the catalogue.
Saros series number from the catalogue.
Type code of the eclipse in the catalogue. Lunar codes start with N, P or T, and solar codes with P, A, T or H. Some codes carry a suffix.
Gamma from the catalogue. It is the least distance between the axis of the shadow and the centre of the Earth or of the Moon.
Magnitude of the eclipse from the catalogue. For a lunar eclipse it is the umbral magnitude, which is negative for a penumbral eclipse.
Penumbral magnitude of a lunar eclipse, from the catalogue. Empty for solar eclipses.
Umbral magnitude of a lunar eclipse, from the catalogue. Empty for solar eclipses.
Duration of the penumbral phase of a lunar eclipse, from the catalogue. Empty for solar eclipses.
Duration of the partial phase of a lunar eclipse. Empty when the eclipse has no partial phase or is solar.
Duration of the total phase of a lunar eclipse. Empty when the eclipse has no total phase or is solar.
Latitude from the catalogue. For a solar eclipse it is the point of greatest eclipse. For a lunar eclipse it is the point where the Moon is in the zenith at greatest eclipse.
East longitude of the same point as greatest_lat. West longitudes are negative.
Version label of the local calculation. Always babylon-local-eclipse-v2.
Latitude of Babylon in the local calculation, 32 degrees 32 minutes 30 seconds north, after Pedersen.
East longitude of Babylon in the local calculation, 44 degrees 25 minutes 30 seconds.
Altitude of Babylon in the local calculation. Always 0, so the horizon is geometric.

Local visibility at Babylon over three Delta T trials, the catalogue value and one standard error either side. robust_visible means visible in all three, robust_not_visible in none and delta_t_sensitive in some.

Lowest phase visible at Babylon over the trials in which the eclipse is visible. Values are penumbral, partial and total for lunar eclipses, and partial, annular, hybrid and total for solar eclipses. Empty when no trial is visible.
Magnitude at Babylon at local maximum, in the trial with the catalogue Delta T. Swiss Ephemeris computes it. Empty when that trial is not visible.
Smallest local magnitude over the visible trials. Empty when no trial is visible.
Largest local magnitude over the visible trials. Empty when no trial is visible.
Apparent altitude of the eclipsed body at local maximum, in the trial with the catalogue Delta T. The body is the Moon, or the Sun for a solar eclipse.
Julian Date in Universal Time of the local maximum at Babylon, in the trial with the catalogue Delta T.
Flags that Swiss Ephemeris returns for the local eclipse in the trial with the catalogue Delta T. It is 0 when that trial is not visible.
True if the eclipse is visible at Babylon with Delta T one standard error below the catalogue value.
True if the eclipse is visible at Babylon with the catalogue Delta T. It is one trial only. local_status and agreement_eligible combine all three.
True if the eclipse is visible at Babylon with Delta T one standard error above the catalogue value.
True if a clause of the stated type can agree with this eclipse. A lunar eclipse needs a partial or total phase visible in all three trials. A solar eclipse needs visibility in all three trials.
Short English reason for agreement_eligible.
Name of the Normal Star with its Greek letter, such as η Piscium. Clauses use the same names.
Greek letter of the star, spelled out, such as eta.
Constellation of the star in the genitive, such as Piscium.
Ecliptic longitude of the star in the fixed J2000 ecliptic. It is the mean of the three epochs of the ADART I table, each reduced to J2000.
Ecliptic latitude of the star in the fixed J2000 ecliptic, the mean of the three reduced epochs.
ADsD identifier of the record. The file holds one row per clause of a Moon or planet against a Normal Star with a month and a day.
Published year of the record, at which the code measures the residual.
Body that the clause measures against the star. Values are moon, mercury, venus, mars, jupiter and saturn.
Normal Star of the clause.
True if the clause states above or below. The code then tests only that the body is near the star in longitude.

Smallest difference in J2000 longitude between the body and the place that the clause states. The code searches a window of 2.5 days around the stated day. The place is the star longitude plus the signed stated distance, at 2 degrees a cubit.
Quantile of the training residuals that sets the tolerance, 0.75, 0.9 or 1.0. Each appearance has one row per quantile.
Planet of the first or last appearance.
Kind of appearance, first or last.

Factor for the signed elongation of the planet from the Sun, so that the expected elongation is positive. It is 1 for an appearance in the west and minus 1 for one in the east. For an outer planet with no stated side, it is minus 1 for a first and 1 for a last appearance.
Median of orientation times elongation over the training appearances of this body, kind and orientation. The training appearances are those of the testable_checked cohort.
Tolerance on the elongation, the larger of 2 degrees and the quantile of the training residuals.
Number of training appearances of this body, kind and orientation.
ADsD identifier of the record of the appearance.
Cohort of the record, from corpus/cohorts.parquet. The testable cohort is the held-out check.
Smallest difference between orientation times elongation and the threshold, within 1.5 days of the stated date in the published year.
True if gap is at most tolerance. The paper reports that this held-out check failed, so the rules do not test appearance dates.
ADsD identifier of the record.
Position of the clause in the parser output of the record, from 0. benchmark_clause_bits.parquet and review_changes.csv use the same numbering.
Offset where the passage of the clause starts in the text column of corpus/tablets.parquet, from 0.
Offset where the passage of the clause ends in that text. The end is exclusive.
Line labels of the edition that the passage touches, as a list of strings.
One line label, such as o 5'.
Passage of the translation that the parser read for the clause.
Full translation of the lines that the passage touches.
Transliteration of the same lines.
SHA-256 of the translation of the record that the parser read.
Name of the parser rule that read the clause, such as measured_normal_star. The suffix _bracket means that the rule read the clause only by ignoring the brackets of the edition.

Origin of the parser rule, from a fixed table in the code. Examples are local_deterministic_parser, published_scheme_sachs_1952, and agent_suggested_X300963_generalized for a rule that the development agent proposed and the authors generalized.

Clause type. appulse is a Moon or planet against a Normal Star, and planet_appulse is the Moon against a planet. planet_planet_appulse is a planet against a planet, and station_appulse is a station against a Normal Star. station is a station in a sign, in_sign is a planet in a sign, and entry is a planet that reaches a sign. first_app and last_app are a first and a last appearance, and acronychal is an acronychal rising. eclipse is an eclipse, season is a solstice or equinox, and sirius is a Sirius date.
Body of the clause. Values are moon, mercury, venus, mars, jupiter and saturn. sun marks a solstice or equinox, sirius a Sirius date, and lunar or solar an eclipse.
Planet that the clause measures the body against, for planet_appulse and planet_planet_appulse. Empty otherwise.
Normal Star of the clause, named as in physical/normal_stars.parquet. Empty when the clause has no star.
Zodiacal sign of the clause, such as Leo. Empty when the clause has no sign.
Babylonian month that governs the clause, I to XII, VI2 or XII2. VI|VI2 means that the tools test both. Empty when no month governs it.
Day of the Babylonian month from the governing day heading. Empty when no day governs the clause. The file stores it as a float.
Number of year changes in the tablet before the clause, 0, 1 or 2. The tools test the clause in the candidate year plus this number.
Stated distance in cubits, at 24 fingers to the cubit, whatever the unit of the text. Empty when the clause states no distance.
Unit words of the stated distance as the text writes them. Values are cubit, cubits, finger, fingers and cubit+finger. Empty when the clause states no distance.
Direction of the stated distance. Values are above, below, in front of and behind. Empty when the clause states no distance.
Side of a station against a Normal Star, east or west. The code treats east as the start of retrograde motion and west as the start of direct motion. Empty otherwise.
Evidence families of the clause, as a list of strings. The clocks are mars, jupiter, saturn, lunar_eclipse and seasonal_sirius, the solar year. moon, venus, mercury and solar are not clocks.
One evidence family. A joint statement lists each of its planets, and a Moon to planet distance lists the planet.
Linked sign positions of a joint statement, as a list of planet and sign pairs. An example is Saturn and Mars were in Leo. The tools test the pairs as one claim. Empty list otherwise.
One planet and sign pair of the joint statement, such as saturn and Leo.
Offset where the passage of the joint statement starts in the translation. It is -1 when the clause is not part of one.
Offset where the passage of the joint statement ends, exclusive. It is -1 when the clause is not part of one.
Day that governs a joint statement. Empty for every row of this file.
Key of the source statement of the clause, as a list. Clauses with the same key form one source statement, which counts once in N_C and in the safety set.
One element of the key. A single clause has atomic and its statement_index. A joint statement has joint, its offsets, its planet and sign pairs, its month, its day and its year_offset.

Expected longitude of the body minus that of the star or planet, at 2 degrees a cubit. It is positive for behind, negative for in front of, and 0 for above or below. Empty when the clause states no distance.
True if the direction is above or below. The rule then tests only that the body lies within the tolerance of the longitude of the reference.

True if the clause is restored in the edition. This is so when its body, sign, star, number, unit or direction lies in brackets. It is also so when the parser read it only through brackets, or when it needs a day number or month numeral that is restored.
True if the scribe marks the event as unobserved, for example with I did not watch. The verdict of such a clause is untestable.
How the clause got its month. explicit_surviving_heading means a month heading, inferred_immediately_preceding_summary the summary rule, and missing_or_lost no month.
Tier of the clause from its type and text alone, decisive or supporting. Only decisive clauses decide which years stay in the strict set.
Text of the clause as the parser normalizes it.
All Babylonian months that the record names, as a list of strings. The tools test a clause without a month over these months.
One month numeral, such as VI or XII2.
Copy of bce_first of corpus/tablets.parquet. The code joins it only after the parser has read every clause. The file stores it as a float.
Copy of bce_second of corpus/tablets.parquet. The file stores it as a float.
Verdict of the clause at the published year. Values are agree, contradict and untestable. not_evaluated marks a record without a published year.
Short English text from the rule that explains the verdict at the published year.
SHA-256 of tools/statements.py, the parser and rules that produced the clauses.
ADsD identifier of the record.
Position of the clause in the reviewed clause list of the record, from 0, in order of the passage. It differs from statement_index of parser_clauses.parquet, because the search inserts clauses.

SHA-256 over the hashes of the code and the physical tables that set the verdicts. It is the same for every row.

Action that the model first proposed, KEEP, MODIFY or DROP. In this run it is always MODIFY.
Action after the checks. MODIFY means that at least one field change passed. KEEP means that the clause stays as the parser read it.
Verdict of the second call that confirms a DROP. Empty in this run, because the model proposed no drop.
Reason that the confirming call gives for a DROP. Empty in this run, because the model proposed no drop.
Field of the clause that the text contradicts, as the confirming call names it. Empty in this run, because the model proposed no drop.

Reasons why code rejected the DROP, joined into one text. Empty in this run, because the model proposed no drop.
Explanation of the confirming call. Empty in this run, because the model proposed no drop.
Result of the second call that confirms each field change of a MODIFY, with the checks of code. Empty when no field change needed this call.
List of decisions, one for each proposed field change.
Field of the proposed change, such as day, month, restored or event_subtype.
Final decision on the change, ACCEPT or REJECT.
Reason code. explicit_source_support supports an accepted change. no_positive_support and inherited_context_protected reject a change.
Exact passage that supports an accepted change. Empty for a rejected change.

Passage that the model cited when code rejected its ACCEPT. Present only in such decisions.
